Subject: Latency targets for Hosted API — need p50/p95 and measurement window

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the demo last week — the Hosted API looks great. Before we move to a PO I need to align our SREs and procurement on latency commitments. A few specific asks:
- Can you confirm p50 and p95 numbers (per-request) for short completions (<=512 tokens) on the Hosted API?
- How do you measure those percentiles (rolling window, aggregation buckets)?
- Are there standard carve-outs for onboarding or platform migrations (we expect traffic burst during initial sync)?

We ran a quick baseline against your hosted endpoint and saw p50~95ms, p95~620ms over a 48h sample (attached csv). Our procurement is pushing for a p95 <= 350ms but engineering realizes that may be aggressive for our workload.

Can you propose the SLA language (measurement window, sample exclusions, and any temporary exception language) so we can take it to legal?

Thanks,
Evan Brooks
Head of Platform, Fintech.ai

Subject: Re: Latency targets for Hosted API — need p50/p95 and measurement window

Hi Evan — really appreciate the data and the quick test. High level proposal below; happy to iterate.

Proposed Hosted API latency commitments (for standard small-completion workloads <=512 tokens):
- p50: 110 ms
- p95: 480 ms
Measurement approach:
- Percentiles computed on service egress latency (time from request receipt to final token egress) for successful responses only.
- Aggregation: per-request latencies bucketed into 1-hour buckets, percentiles computed per bucket, then rolled up into a 30-day trailing window for SLA evaluation.
- Exclusions: scheduled maintenance windows (scheduled 48+ hours in advance), customer-triggered load tests, and external network timeouts.

Exception / onboarding carve-out suggestion:
- For customers in onboarding (first 60 days after production cutover), Redwood will apply a temporary p95 allowance of up to 540 ms (no credit) while telemetry stabilizes. If p95 remains >540 ms after 60 days, we will (a) provide a remediation plan and (b) consider a one-time service credit if RCA shows platform-side regressions.

I've attached a draft SLA snippet (proposed_sla_draft.pdf) for legal. If you want a tighter p95 (e.g., 350 ms) we can propose a commercial commitment tied to Reserved Capacity (Dedicated) or a custom performance plan.

Next steps: are you open to a 60-day onboarding carve-out, and can we loop procurement/Legal?

Best,
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Thanks for the summary. A few technical clarifications and constraints from runtime:
- Measurement: agree on egress latency for successful responses. We compute percentiles from raw request traces and roll up into 1h buckets; the math Soojin suggested (hourly buckets -> 30-day trailing) is feasible.
- Sampling & retries: we need to exclude client-side retries and requests that hit our internal gateway error (5xx) from p95 calculations; those are counted against availability instead.
- Regional variance: p95 for EU and APAC regions can be ~15-30% higher depending on model and peering; if Fintech.ai needs a global p95 of 350 ms we should scope traffic (e.g., US-only) or recommend Dedicated in-region.
- Observability: we can provide a read-only dashboard and a streaming trace feed for the first 30 days; we will also run a synthetic load test prior to cutover to baseline expected percentiles.

I attached the measurement spec with the exact percentiles algorithm and exclusion rules: latency-measurement-spec.md

Karthik
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime

Hi Evan — thanks for the patience while we validated internally. Final proposed language below (we can include this as an SLA exhibit):

1) Committed Latency Targets (small completions <=512 tokens, US region):
   - p50: 110 ms
   - p95: 480 ms

2) Measurement and Windowing:
   - Latency is measured at service egress for successful responses.
   - Percentiles are computed on 1-hour latency buckets and evaluated over a 30-day trailing window for SLA compliance.
   - Exclusions: scheduled maintenance (>=48h notice), customer-triggered load tests, and client-side network timeouts. 5xx errors are excluded from percentile latency and counted under availability metrics.

3) Onboarding Exception:
   - For the first 60 calendar days following customer production cutover, Redwood will apply a temporary p95 allowance up to 540 ms (no service credit).
   - Redwood will provide observability access (read-only dashboards + streaming traces) and perform one synthetic load test before cutover.
   - At day 45 Redwood and Fintech.ai will review telemetry and agree on next steps; if p95 remains >540 ms due to platform issues, Redwood will provide a remediation plan and may grant a one-time service credit at its discretion.

If Fintech.ai needs a commercial commitment for p95 <= 350 ms, we recommend Dedicated (reserved, in-region capacity) and we can provide an addendum with tighter targets and associated pricing.

Next steps:
- Reply with approval of the 60-day carve-out and we will convert the language into an SLA exhibit and send for DocuSign.
- If you want a shorter carve-out (30 days) or different thresholds, tell us and we will run numbers with engineering.

Thanks,
